tasks.name: Build e2e mapping table: smoke.sh + smoke.ps1 sections
tasks.description:
Build the section-by-section coverage mapping table for tests/smoke.sh and tests/smoke.ps1 — the coverage-proof artifact every later port task and acceptance check references. This is the FIRST task in the PRD; it creates the shared mapping table file.

Location: create dev/local/designs/00171-migrate-shell-scenarios-to-e2e-v1-mapping.md (new file; durable PRD satellite — not deleted by dev/local GC, dies only when the PRD itself moves to done/). Source files: tests/smoke.sh (769 lines, ~56 numbered section headers via `rg -n "^# [0-9]" tests/smoke.sh`), tests/smoke.ps1 (932 lines, ~56 numbered section headers, near-mirror dialect of smoke.sh).

Reuse: cross-check each candidate target against the existing tests/e2e/*.rs suite (100+ files, `rg -n "fn " tests/e2e/*.rs` for an index) before assigning a NEW target test name — if an existing e2e test already covers the same assertion, the row must say "ALREADY COVERED by <test>", never a duplicate.

Contract (verbatim from the design doc's Interfaces & contracts):
- Mapping table row format: "one row per shell section: file:line | section # | target e2e test (or \"ALREADY COVERED by <existing test>\" or \"justified survivor: <reason>\") | needs server? | must-fail? | status"
- Test naming: "smoke_NN_slug / integration_NN_slug, NN zero-padded to match the source section number (04, not 4)."
- Must-fail idiom (for must-fail rows' target-test note): the shell `ddb-fails` helper / bash bare `!` negation maps to `assert_cmd`'s `.assert().failure().stderr(predicate::str::contains("error:"))`, already used in tests/e2e/cli_update_app_error.rs — reuse verbatim, do not invent a new pattern.

Details:
- Enumerate every numbered section in both files by file:line. Read each section body (not just the header) to determine what it asserts.
- For each section: assign a target Rust test name (smoke_NN_slug), note whether it needs ServerGuard (a live `ddb serve`) or is CLI-only, whether it is a must-fail scenario, and set status to TODO.
- tests/smoke.ps1 is invoked by NO workflow today (absent from both test.yml and full-validation.yml, confirmed by grep) — still map its sections per the PRD's 100%-coverage metric; note the zero-CI-risk fact in that row's notes rather than skipping the section.
- Where smoke.sh and smoke.ps1 carry the same NN section as dialect mirrors of one scenario, they share ONE target Rust test — do not create two target rows pointing at two different tests for the same scenario; note "dialect pair, same target" in the row.
- Every section must map to a target row — zero unmapped sections is the acceptance bar.

Acceptance criteria:
- the table is complete with zero unmapped sections (duplicate-numbered sections disambiguated by file:line); it lives in the PRD workdir notes and is referenced by later acceptance checks.

Verify: row count in the new mapping table (smoke section) matches the combined section count from `rg -c "^# [0-9]" tests/smoke.sh tests/smoke.ps1` (accounting for shared dialect-pair rows counting once each per file, not merged into a single row); spot-check 3 random rows against their source line to confirm accuracy.
